doom.driver: Iran claims four tankers struck mines in Hormuz as strike fears grow after U.S. midterms
doom.blurb: FOUR TANKERS STRICKEN IN THE WATERS OF HORMUZ
doom.summary: Four tankers hitting mines in Hormuz, while Tehran and Washington argue over whether the shipping lanes are clear, is a strange way to celebrate the oil market 'easing.' Elsewhere, someone walked off with $6.3 billion from Binance via one DevOps laptop, and a contractor's personal Claude agent spent two months loose on a Pentagon network. Meanwhile Xi is emptying Politburo seats at a record pace, which is never a sign of a relaxed autumn.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: A report says Trump ignored intelligence about a Chinese spy close to Jensen Huang, the Pentagon IG declines to examine the Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, and the midterms are days away.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Mines in Hormuz amid post-midterm strike fears, Ukraine sending more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight, record CCP purges, and Israel deadlocked with its PM calling the election stolen.

factors.detail: The biggest crypto heist on record, a leak exposing 41,000 DHS staff and undercover ICE agents, and wildfire smoke blamed for 3,500 deaths in Indonesia.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A night scene on the Iranian shore of the Strait of Hormuz in the hours before dawn, looking across a black, oily sea from a rocky quay on Qeshm Island. The sky is deep black, with a thin band of blood-orange glow low on the horizon. Faint volcanic underlighting rims the red, mineral-streaked cliffs of Hormuz Island across the water. In the far distance, the smeared orange glow of a smoldering tanker hull sits low on the sea. It is small, silent and unverified, with no flames shown, only a dull ember and a drifting ribbon of smoke. The aftermath is a harbor waiting through a tense calm. In the foreground, a weathered concrete fishing quay is lit by one sodium-orange streetlamp. Wooden dhows and small fishing boats are moored and idle, their nets coiled and piled on the stones. A single bearded fisherman in a dark jacket and white cap stands whole and still at the quay edge, his back to us, staring out at the distant glow. Beside him, a row of orange-and-black marker buoys has been dragged ashore, dripping, with a coil of rope and a boat hook laid neatly across them. On a crate sits a small battered radio with a faintly glowing dial, and a steaming tea glass with a tiny orange highlight. Behind the quay, a shuttered fish market has a half-raised metal shutter and one weak orange bulb inside. Shadows pool deep and black beneath the hulls. The orange reflections on the wet stone and the dark water break up into chunky pixel dithering. Cool tones are almost extinguished, leaving only blood orange and deep black with a few ember-red accents.

minor: The fisherman is a dark silhouette with almost no detail. His legs are thick and column-like, and his white cap reads as a pale blob. This is acceptable in the shadow.
The buoys are stacked in a row and look more like barrels or pumpkins than marker buoys. The rope and boat hook are hard to tell apart, and the boat hook is barely visible.
The moored boats on the right are dark and tangled together, so masts, rigging and hulls blur into each other. They are lost in shadow and not obviously broken.
The radio and tea glass sit on a dark crate or block. The block's perspective is a little muddy, but both objects are readable.
The tanker on the horizon is only a tiny dark shape with a smoke trail, and the cliffs are stylized. This matches the prompt's intent.
The shuttered fish market on the left is murky, with a vague interior and no clear half-raised shutter. It has no readable text.

dawn.driver: Venezuela opposition leader María Machado calls for elections upon return. Machado, who was in exile for nearly a year, said the transition in Venezuela's government would be "irreversible, organised, pacific".
dawn.blurb: A FAIRLY HOPEFUL RETURN FOR VENEZUELA
dawn.summary: María Corina Machado is back on Venezuelan soil after nearly a year away, calling for elections and promising a transition that will be "irreversible, organised, pacific." Those three words carry a whole country's hopes for a calm, democratic road ahead. Elsewhere, chemists have found a plant-inspired alternative to forever chemicals that keeps the non-stick magic but breaks down cleanly, and the tiniest patients at Cleveland Clinic Children's Hospital wore their very first Halloween costumes.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: A mouse study suggests the body's ability to regrow nerves can be switched back on by inhaling carbon dioxide, hinting at new routes to healing.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Machado's homecoming comes with a pledge of an organised, peaceful transition and a call to let Venezuelans choose their leaders at the ballot box.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: NICU babies in Cleveland celebrated their first Halloween in tiny costumes, a sweet milestone for families and nurses alike.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Researchers borrowed a trick from plant biology to create a durable, non-stick coating that doesn't linger in the environment the way PFAS do.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A beautifully preserved 700,000-year-old elephant tooth from northern Israel reveals a lush ancient world where giant elephants and early humans lived side by side.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. GROUND-LEVEL VIEW looking steeply upward from the cobbles of a narrow Caracas apartment-block street in clear golden-yellow morning daylight and fresh green, with balanced, steady warmth. Tall pastel-yellow and ochre concrete apartment towers lean in on both sides, their balconies hung with potted green plants and drying laundry. Between them a wide strip of pale blue sky opens above, and the sun's golden light spills down the facades. Fresh green tropical trees and the green slopes of El Ávila rise at the far end of the street. On a third-floor balcony in the foreground, seen whole from below and leaning on the railing, an elderly Venezuelan woman in a simple yellow cardigan listens to a small radio held against her chest. Her eyes are bright and wet, and she wears a calm, quietly hopeful half-smile. Beside her stands a young man in a plain white shirt, completely visible, holding a passport in one hand and a folded paper ballot in the other. He gazes up and out at the sky with a relieved, steady expression, as if he is considering coming home. Their open balcony door behind them shows a warm interior with a table set for two. A tiny, faint, dark speedboat shape appears only as a small framed photograph on the balcony wall. Far below at the street's edge, a few small neighbors, all whole, stand peacefully at their doorways with their faces tilted up. A string of yellow, blue and red paper bunting runs across the gap between the buildings, framing the sky. The street itself stays calm, with no crowds or speeches shown, so the event is only implied by the quiet faces of the people it touches.

minor: The radio the woman holds against her chest is a small dark clump that doesn't clearly read as a radio.
The folded ballot in the young man's hand is a vague white shape.
The framed photo on the balcony wall looks like a blue landscape, not a speedboat. This is hard to notice.
The interior behind the balcony is dark, and the table set for two isn't visible.
The distant neighbors in the doorways are small and simply drawn, but they read as whole people.
The laundry on the right-hand balconies is blocky and blends into the facades.
